correctness.rationale: For each lambda the three nonzero Artin–Schreier classes have reduced odd pole order 5, hence give independent quadratic characters, connected Klein-four cover, three genus-two quotients, and conductor-different genus g=6. The nontrivial character eigenspaces factor its degree-12 Weil numerator into the three genus-two quartics. Independent exact trace enumeration of all 4 and 16 possible x in F4 and F16 yielded quotient (N1,N2)=(5,33) universally for the first factor, (5,33)/(5,9)/(7,21) for the second and third as lambda varies, recovering E=Phi4(2T)^2, B=Phi12(2T), D=Phi5(2T). Multiplication yields the stated P_lambda and P_lambda(1) rational Jacobian orders. Powered eigenvalue multisets with orders 4,12,5 combined with the Tate finite-field isogeny criterion force and suffice for multiples of 3,20,60, respectively, not just the degrees tested numerically. This argument proves all positive r, whereas the finite enumeration proves only each requisite F4/F16 table entry.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified. Almeida Filho–Tafazolian–Vieira (2026) Proposition 10.4 defines exactly this genus-six family and proves supersingularity and a-number; Proposition 10.6 classifies Ekedahl–Oort types, but the inspected full source contains no zeta-function computation or minimal isogeny extensions. Maisner–Nart (2004) comprehensively classify supersingular genus-two Weil polynomials, so the quotient ingredient is prior art. The assessed additional fact is the complete coupled four-parameter genus-six Frobenius spectra and sharp pairwise extension degrees, which distinguish rational types within one geometric Ekedahl–Oort stratum. Equivalent unindexed computation remains possible.
